summary: Adolf Kießling worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker (~1855–1858) and held posts at the University of Basel (~1869–1877), University of Greifswald (~1877–1889), and University of Göttingen (~1889–1893).

Adolf Kirchhoff worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (1842–1846) under Karl Lachmann and August Boeckh. He held posts at Joachimsthalsches Gymnasium (1846) and Humboldt University/Frederick William University Berlin (1865–1907).

Adolphe Regnier worked in Indology, linguistics, history, and archaeology, studying under Eugène Burnouf. He held positions at the Collège de France (1838), École Normale Supérieure (1841–1843), Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres (1855), and the Palace of Fontainebleau (1873).

Adrian Zenz specializes in Tibetology and Sinology. He earned a master's at the University of Auckland (~2000–2001) and a Ph.D. at Cambridge under Hildegard Diemberger (~2006–2010). His posts include the European School of Culture and Theology and Victims of Communism Memorial Foundation.

Agata Bareja-Starzyńska works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She conducted research at the University of Oslo (1993) and University of Bonn (1995), and held a post attested at the University of Warsaw in 2008.

Agathon Benary worked in linguistics. He studied at the University of Göttingen and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1824–1827), and under Franz Bopp (~1827–1830). He later held posts at Köllnisches Gymnasium (1833–1860) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1839).

Agehananda Bharati was a scholar in religious studies and Indology who studied at the University of Vienna (~1945–1948). He taught in India, Japan, and the United States, notably serving as Ford-Maxwell Professor of South Asian Studies at Syracuse University (1961–1991).

Agnieszka Helman-Ważny works in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She studied at the Academy of Fine Arts, Warsaw (~1996–2001) and Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń (~2002–2007). She held affiliations at Cornell University (~2008–2010) and the University of Warsaw (2015).

Agvan Dorzhiev was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Drepung Monastery and Drepung Gomang Dratsang (1873, 1880–1888), earning a Geshe Lharampa degree. He founded Datsan Gunzechoinei and Atsagat Datsan (1913) and taught the 13th Dalai Lama.

Ahmad Hasan Dani worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and the University of London under Anant Sadashiv Altekar, Kenneth de Burgh Codrington, and Mortimer Wheeler, holding posts at Dhaka, Peshawar, and Quaid-i-Azam universities.
Aiko Okoshi worked in philosophy and religious studies. She studied at Kyoto University from approximately 1970 to 1975, and held an academic appointment at Kindai University beginning in 1990.

Ajahn Amaro is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Bedford College, London (~1974–1977) and under Ajahn Chah and Ajahn Sumedho. He served as co-abbot of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery (~1996–2010) and became abbot of Amaravati Buddhist Monastery in 2010.

Ajahn Brahm is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Emmanuel College, University of Cambridge (~1969–1972) and under Boonman Poonsuwan and Ajahn Chah (~1975–1983). He has served as abbot of Bodhinyana Monastery since around 1984.

Ajahn Maha Somchai Kusalacitto is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Madras and served as dean and deputy rector for foreign affairs at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, attested in 2003.

Ajahn Pasanno is active in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Ajahn Chah from around 1974 to 1982 and served as the founding co-abbot of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery from around 1996 to 2018.
Ajahn Sucitto is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the University of Warwick (~1968–1971) and trained under Ajahn Sumedho (1977). He served as abbot of Cittaviveka from 1992 to 2014.

Ajahn Sumedho is a Buddhist studies figure who earned degrees at the University of Washington and UC Berkeley (~1961–1963) and trained under Ajahn Chah (1967–1977). He served as abbot of Wat Pa Nanachat (1975) and Amaravati Buddhist Monastery (1984–2010).
Ajit Ranjan Bhattacharyya was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya and held a position at the University of Calcutta as an Ex-Puranchand Nahar Fellow.

Akifumi Naito is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University, Honganji Sōgakuin, and under Gadjin M. Nagao. He held posts at Ryukoku University (attested 2003–2009), Jodo Shinshu Institute, Kyoto Women's University, and Gyoshin Buddhist Academy.

Akihiko Akamatsu specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Paris/Sorbonne Nouvelle under Yuichi Kajiyama. His career includes posts at Kyushu University (1987) and Kyoto University as professor and vice president (1983–2023).
